root_causes.macos: Tauri completed and uploaded each DMG, then removed bundle/macos/*.app. The old post-build verifier searched only for the removed intermediate app and failed before inspecting the shipped DMG.
root_causes.windows: The Windows application and NSIS installer built successfully. The combined job then failed while WiX light.exe linked the MSI on windows-2025; Tauri documents VBSCRIPT as an MSI/WiX prerequisite and the runner did not expose a diagnostic beyond failed to run light.exe.

changes: Verify the exact app inside the generated DMG by mounting read-only, copying with ditto, then running plist, architecture, code-signature, dynamic-library, and native launch checks.
Split Windows NSIS and MSI into independent matrix jobs so one installer can never hide the result of the other.
Pin Windows installer jobs to windows-2022 and smoke-test VBSCRIPT before invoking the WiX MSI linker.
Add post-build NSIS silent install/uninstall and MSI administrative-image verification.
Harden the WiX desktop shortcut component with a registry key path rooted under TARGETDIR.
Use deterministic ASCII release asset names and keep draft-first atomic publication until two DMGs, one MSI, and one NSIS EXE exist.
Add a Linux-executable regression harness proving the macOS wrapper falls back from a removed intermediate app to the app contained in a DMG.

environment_blocked_not_passed: Fresh npm ci and the complete 114-test JavaScript suite could not be repeated in this network-isolated packaging container. The same runtime suite passed 114/114 on the user Mac and in the preceding hosted CI before the native-release-only edits.
Full Python collection is blocked locally by missing pycrdt and fakeredis. The per-file matrix records these as blocked, never as passed.
Rust fmt/clippy/test and native Tauri DMG/MSI/NSIS builds require Cargo and hosted macOS/Windows runners, which are unavailable in this container.
PowerShell execution of the Windows installer verifier requires a Windows runner.
